name: Bharatanatyam
notes: Bharatanatyam FOUNDATION pack (Doc 04 template) — deliberately a doorway, not a syllabus. The honesty this pack is built around: bharatanatyam is a classical art transmitted through the GURU-SHISHYA tradition — years of embodied correction from a teacher — and an app cannot be that. So this pack teaches what CAN be honestly self-trained (tala literacy, the conditioning araimandi demands, the history) and places every movement node behind a hard honesty gate that says so. The history is told with care because it must be: the dance descends from sadir, the temple-and-court art of the DEVADASI communities of Tamil Nadu — hereditary women artists who were dispossessed when colonial-era 'anti-nautch' campaigns and the 1947 Madras Devadasis Act criminalized their practice. The 20th-century renaissance that made bharatanatyam a global classical form is credited where it belongs — E. Krishna Iyer's advocacy, Rukmini Devi Arundale's Kalakshetra — AND the pack keeps visible what that renaissance cost: the art moved largely out of the hereditary communities' hands, and masters like T. Balasaraswati carried the devadasi lineage's own artistry forward against that tide. Adi tala rides in this app's Rhythm Trainer with its sollukattu noted. Knees are protected: araimandi is conditioned progressively, never forced.

seasons.finale: Film yourself clapping adi tala through one full cycle set — the eight counted aloud, the claps landing true.
Write five sentences in your journal: what sadir was, what happened to the devadasis, and who carried the art forward — in your own words.
Film your araimandi conditioning: the half-sit held with tall spine for 30 seconds, knees tracking over toes, no pain.
Film the tatta adavu study — strikes with the tala counted aloud — labeled honestly as pre-teacher practice.
Contact a bharatanatyam teacher — a local school or an online guru-led program. The tradition's real door; this pack exists to walk you to it.

attributes.name: Araimandi legs L1
attributes.test: 3 × 30s half-sit holds (feet turned out, heels together, knees over toes, spine tall) with full rest between — built gradually over weeks, never through knee pain

attributes.name: Tala hands L1
attributes.test: clap adi tala's 8-beat cycle with its claps and waves for two minutes without losing the count — the dance's clock, installed

attributes.name: Tall-spine posture L1
attributes.test: 60s standing with lifted chest, level chin, shoulders wide and down — bharatanatyam's carriage begins before any step

nodes.name: Adi tala & sollukattu — the dance's clock
checkpoints: adi tala is the 8-beat cycle most beginner adavus ride — counted with claps, finger counts and waves; it's in this app's Rhythm Trainer
sollukattu are the spoken syllables — 'tai ya tai hi' and their kin — that the nattuvanar recites to conduct the dance; the syllables ARE the choreography's rhythm spoken aloud
learn to keep tala with your hands while speaking a simple sollukattu — musicianship the guru will expect on day one

nodes.name: The Carnatic frame & the margam
checkpoints: bharatanatyam lives inside Carnatic music — vocalist, mridangam, violin or veena, and the nattuvanar's cymbals
a full recital traditionally follows the margam — a sequence from alarippu through varnam to tillana — an arc the devadasi tradition's own musicians and nattuvanars shaped
listen to one full varnam this season; the dance makes sense at the speed of its music

nodes.name: Sadir & the devadasis — the root, told honestly
checkpoints: bharatanatyam descends from sadir, the art of the DEVADASI communities of Tamil Nadu — hereditary women artists dedicated to temples and courts, who held the dance, its music and its repertoire for centuries

colonial-era 'anti-nautch' campaigns stigmatized these women, and the 1947 Madras Devadasis (Prevention of Dedication) Act ended their practice — the community that made the art was dispossessed of it
this history is not a footnote; dancers today increasingly name it on stage, and this pack asks the same of you

nodes.name: The renaissance — credited, and complicated
checkpoints: the 1930s renaissance is credited where it belongs: E. Krishna Iyer fought the ban's stigma in public and on stage, and Rukmini Devi Arundale's Kalakshetra (1936) rebuilt the art as 'bharatanatyam' and carried it to the world
the renaissance was also complicated: as the renamed art entered new hands, the hereditary community was largely displaced from it — credit and cost belong in the same sentence

T. Balasaraswati — of the devadasi hereditary lineage itself — stands among the form's greatest artists, carrying her family's banis and its abhinaya to the world stage; know her name alongside the revivalists'

nodes.name: The guru gate — what an app cannot teach
checkpoints: the guru-shishya tradition holds this dance: years of embodied correction — the angle of a wrist, the weight of a glance — passed teacher to student; no app replaces that, including this one
everything movement-shaped past this gate is PRE-TEACHER PRACTICE: tala literacy, conditioning, and study-sketches of first exercises, honestly labeled
the pass condition for this node is saying it back in your own words: what can self-training give you here, and what can only a guru give?

nodes.name: Araimandi — conditioning the half-sit
nodes.anchor: the posture the whole dance stands in
checkpoints: araimandi: heels together, feet turned out, knees bent wide over the toes, spine tall — the half-sit bharatanatyam lives in
condition it progressively: short holds, full rest, weeks of patience — turnout comes from the hips, never wrenched from the knees
a mirror check per hold: knees tracking over toes, pelvis neutral, chest lifted — the guru will rebuild the details; arrive with healthy joints and honest habits
mistakes: forcing depth or turnout through knee pain (nothing in this pack is worth a meniscus; shallower and correct wins)

nodes.name: Tatta adavu — the first strikes (study)
checkpoints: tatta adavu — flat-foot strikes in araimandi to 'tai ya tai hi' — is traditionally the first adavu a guru teaches; here it is a STUDY: feel the tala in the feet, keep the posture honest
strike flat and sound the floor without slamming; the spine does not bounce
practice in three speeds as the tradition does — the same pattern slow, medium, fast — counting aloud
log it as pre-teacher practice; your future guru will rebuild it, and arriving with tala in your feet makes that rebuilding faster

nodes.name: Hasta mudras — the hands' alphabet (study)
checkpoints: the hastas are codified hand gestures — pataka's flat palm, tripataka, ardhachandra's half-moon and their kin — an alphabet the dance spells meaning with
learn to FORM five single-hand hastas cleanly and name them; forming is self-trainable, USING them to speak is the guru's domain
drill them slowly with strong fingers and a soft wrist — mushy hastas are the most common beginner flag

nodes.name: Abhinaya — where the dance becomes speech
checkpoints: abhinaya is expression — face, eyes and gesture telling story and devotion; it is the art's deepest layer and the least self-trainable thing in dance
watch one abhinaya piece by a master (Balasaraswati's recorded work is a monument) and journal what the eyes alone told you
this node is watching-literacy only — abhinaya is learned at a guru's feet, sometimes over decades; knowing that IS the lesson

nodes.name: The daily practice — filmed
checkpoints: film one honest session: tala clapped, araimandi holds, tatta study in two speeds, five hastas formed and named
count aloud on camera — the voice keeping tala is half the discipline
label the video 'pre-teacher practice' and mean it; honesty on the label is this pack's whole architecture

nodes.name: Finding the guru
checkpoints: find a teacher: local bharatanatyam schools, temple-community classes, or established online guru-led programs — many teach absolute beginners of every background and age
arrive with what this pack gave you — tala in your hands, conditioned legs, the history in your mouth — and hand the rest to the tradition that actually holds it
when you perform someday, name the lineage your teacher gives you AND the devadasi communities the art came from; that sentence is this pack's graduation

teachers.name: Bharatanatyam — history including sadir and the devadasi tradition
